title: NearZeroSumGames.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each player's cost is convex in its own decision variable; g is jointly convex on X×Y. X and Y are compact convex sets.

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: For every fixed y, h(·,y) is μ-strongly convex on X; for every fixed x, -h(x,·) is ν-strongly convex on Y. Consequently, the players' own-variable costs have respective strong convexity moduli μ and ν, with 0<μ,ν≤L.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Two-player general-sum Nash equilibrium problem with costs h+g for the x-player and g-h for the y-player. The zero-sum component h is strongly convex-concave, and the shared coupling g is jointly convex. An equilibrium exists.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A feasible query z returns exactly (H_x(z)+G_x(z), -H_y(z)+G_y(z)), the combined vector of players' own gradients. Separate H and G evaluations, cross-player gradients, and function values are not supplied. Replies are independent of call index and seed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NearZeroSumGames.lean: ownGradient and spec.admissible Sum.inl answer clause.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: A query at any ambient point returns its exact Euclidean projection onto X×Y. Projection queries and own-gradient queries each consume one call from the same fixed oracle budget.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NearZeroSumGames.lean: spec.Query, spec.admissible projection inequality and Sum.inr answer clause; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; the product uses the Euclidean ℓ₂ norm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NearZeroSumGames.lean: Public.finiteE, Public.finiteF, Public.innerE, Public.innerF, Space.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Near-zero-sum structure is quantified by the jointly convex coupling's gradient Lipschitz constant δ, where 0≤δ≤L. Both H+G and H-G are L-Lipschitz on the domain. The product domain has diameter at most D>0 and contains the supplied initial point. Spaces, sets, L, μ, ν, δ, D, ε, x0, and y0 are public; h, g, and the witnessing gradient and projection maps are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NearZeroSumGames.lean: Public, Problem, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: There exists an equilibrium zstar such that the returned point satisfies ‖output-zstar‖²≤ε in the product Euclidean norm, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to X×Y.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the squared-distance bound hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed law, for a single equilibrium chosen outside the almost-sure quantifier. The oracle budget is fixed rather than expected.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NearZeroSumGames.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and execute.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup specializes convex Nash games through a shared jointly convex coupling with a separate smoothness parameter δ, while exposing only combined own gradients and counting projections in the same oracle budget.

descriptionHtml:
Near-Zero-Sum Games

We study a two-player game on nonempty compact convex sets X⊂E and Y⊂F, where E,F are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces. The players minimize h+g and g−h, respectively, where h,g:E×F→R. The function h is strongly convex in the first variable and strongly concave in the second; g is jointly convex. Their within-domain gradients satisfy Lipschitz bounds, and an equilibrium exists. The oracle returns the players’ own-variable gradients or a Euclidean projection. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output z¯ with ∥z¯−z⋆∥2≤ε almost surely for one fixed equilibrium z⋆, using the product Euclidean norm.

Write Z=X×Y and equip E×F with the inner product and norm ⟨(x,y),(u,v)⟩=⟨x,u⟩E+⟨y,v⟩F,∥(x,y)∥2=∥x∥E2+∥y∥F2. Define the players’ costs by c1=h+g and c2=g−h. Their respective problems, with the other player’s action fixed, are minx∈Xc1(x,y),miny∈Yc2(x,y). The algorithm receives E,F,X,Y, a feasible starting point z0=(x0,y0), and the parameters L,μ,ν,δ,D,ε, whose ranges are 0<μ≤L,0<ν≤L,0≤δ≤L,D>0,ε>0. The functions h and g are accessed through the oracle described below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible geometry). The sets X and Y are compact and convex, x0∈X, y0∈Y, and ∥z−w∥≤D,z,w∈Z.

Assumption 2 (Game structure). For every t∈[0,1], x,x′∈X, and y,y′∈Y, h((1−t)x+tx′,y)≤(1−t)h(x,y)+th(x′,y)≤−μ2t(1−t)∥x−x′∥E2,h(x,(1−t)y+ty′)≥(1−t)h(x,y)+th(x,y′)≥+ν2t(1−t)∥y−y′∥F2. Moreover, g is jointly convex on Z: for z,w∈Z and t∈[0,1], g((1−t)z+tw)≤(1−t)g(z)+tg(w).

Assumption 3 (Within-domain smoothness). There exist gradient selections H,G:Z→E×F such that, for every z∈Z, as w→z within Z, h(w)−h(z)−⟨H(z),w−z⟩=o(∥w−z∥),g(w)−g(z)−⟨G(z),w−z⟩=o(∥w−z∥). These selections satisfy, for all z,w∈Z, ∥(H+G)(z)−(H+G)(w)∥≤L∥z−w∥,∥(H−G)(z)−(H−G)(w)∥≤L∥z−w∥,∥G(z)−G(w)∥≤δ∥z−w∥.

Assumption 4 (Equilibrium existence). There exists z⋆=(x⋆,y⋆)∈Z such that c1(x⋆,y⋆)≤c1(x,y⋆)for every x∈X,c2(x⋆,y⋆)≤c2(x⋆,y)for every y∈Y. Such a point is a Nash equilibrium.

Write H=(Hx,Hy) and G=(Gx,Gy). At a feasible query z∈Z, the exact game-gradient oracle returns V(z)=(Hx(z)+Gx(z),−Hy(z)+Gy(z)). A projection query may instead be made at any u∈E×F and returns ΠZ(u), characterized by ΠZ(u)∈Z,⟨u−ΠZ(u),w−ΠZ(u)⟩≤0for every w∈Z. Both types of query count toward the same total oracle-call budget.

After the allotted calls, the output must satisfy, for some fixed Nash equilibrium z⋆, z¯∈Z,∥z¯−z⋆∥2≤εP-a.s., where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness and z⋆ is independent of its realization.

comparisonHtml:
Compact convex X⊂E, Y⊂F in finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; feasible initial point; diam(X×Y)≤D. Player costs are h+g and g−h: h is μ-strongly convex in x and ν-strongly concave in y; g is jointly convex. Gradients within the domain exist, ∇(h±g) are L-Lipschitz, and ∇g is δ-Lipschitz. Here 0<μ,ν≤L, 0≤δ≤L, and D,ε>0. An equilibrium exists. Access: own gradients and exact Euclidean projection. Target: feasible zout with ∥zout−z⋆∥2≤ε for an equilibrium z⋆.

Near-zero-sum games: NearZeroSumGames.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) NearZeroSumOwnGradients (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(Lmm+δM+δℓ0ℓ1) own-gradient and projection calls, counted together.
(2) ICL (Luo et al. 2025, Thm. 1) O(Lmm+δM+δℓ0ℓ1) full-utility-gradient queries, ε≤D2. Projections not quantified. (1): Matches rate for ε≤D2 using own gradients instead of full utility gradients; no separate ∇g. Includes projection costs.
(3) Extragradient (Luo et al. 2025, Prop. 1) O(Lmℓ0) own-gradient and projection calls. (1): Faster when m+δM+δℓ12≪1. For δ=m, L=M=κm: O(κℓ0ℓ1) instead of O(κℓ0). (1): Extra factor ℓ1 when M≍m or δ≳M; needs separate curvature and coupling parameters and the decomposition structure.
(4) Zero-sum guarantee (Luo et al. 2025, Prop. 2) O(Lμνℓ0) gradient queries; δ=0 (affine g absorbed into the saddle objective). (1): Scope extends to δ>0. (1): Extra factor ℓ1 on the δ=0 overlap.

Abbr: m=min{μ,ν}, M=max{μ,ν}; log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t}; ℓ0=1+log+⁡(D2/ε), ℓ1=1+log+⁡(L2D2/(m2ε)). Own-gradient query: (∇x(h+g),∇y(g−h)). Full-utility-gradient query: ∇(h+g) and ∇(g−h).

Luo, Ruichen, Sebastian U. Stich, and Krishnendu Chatterjee. 2025. Monotone Near-Zero-Sum Games: A Generalization of Convex-Concave Minimax. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.02690.
source:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Strong
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
import LongTails.Template

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

open OracleTemplate

namespace LongTails.Setups.NearZeroSumGames

structure Public where
  E : Type
  F : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [innerF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [finiteF : FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
  X : Set E
  Y : Set F
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  ν : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  D : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E
  y0 : F

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE
  Public.normedF Public.innerF Public.finiteF

abbrev Space (p : Public) := WithLp 2 (p.E × p.F)

def domain (p : Public) : Set (Space p) := {z | z.fst ∈ p.X ∧ z.snd ∈ p.Y}

def initialPoint (p : Public) : Space p := WithLp.toLp 2 (p.x0, p.y0)

structure Problem (p : Public) where
  h : Space p → ℝ
  g : Space p → ℝ

def IsEquilibrium {p : Public} (I : Problem p) (z : Space p) : Prop :=
  z ∈ domain p ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.X, I.h z + I.g z ≤
      I.h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, z.snd)) + I.g (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, z.snd))) ∧
    (∀ y ∈ p.Y, I.g z - I.h z ≤
      I.g (WithLp.toLp 2 (z.fst, y)) - I.h (WithLp.toLp 2 (z.fst, y)))

def ownGradient {p : Public} (H G : Space p → Space p) (z : Space p) : Space p :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 ((H z).fst + (G z).fst, -(H z).snd + (G z).snd)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance := Problem
  Query p := Space p ⊕ Space p
  Reply p := Space p
  Output p := Space p
  publicInput := id
  valid p :=
    IsCompact p.X ∧ IsCompact p.Y ∧ Convex ℝ p.X ∧ Convex ℝ p.Y ∧
    p.x0 ∈ p.X ∧ p.y0 ∈ p.Y ∧
    (∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p, ‖z - w‖ ≤ p.D) ∧
    0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.ν ∧ p.ν ≤ p.L ∧
    0 ≤ p.δ ∧ p.δ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    (∀ y ∈ p.Y, StrongConvexOn p.X p.μ (fun x => I.h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)))) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ p.X, StrongConvexOn p.Y p.ν (fun y => -I.h (WithLp.toLp 2 (x, y)))) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ (domain p) I.g ∧
    (∃ zstar, IsEquilibrium I zstar) ∧
    ∃ H G P : Space p → Space p,
      (∀ z ∈ domain p, HasGradientWithinAt I.h (H z) (domain p) z) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ domain p, HasGradientWithinAt I.g (G z) (domain p) z) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p,
        ‖(H z + G z) - (H w + G w)‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p,
        ‖(H z - G z) - (H w - G w)‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ domain p, ∀ w ∈ domain p, ‖G z - G w‖ ≤ p.δ * ‖z - w‖) ∧
      (∀ z, P z ∈ domain p ∧ ∀ w ∈ domain p, ⟪z - P z, w - P z⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
      (∀ k seed z, z ∈ domain p →
        oracle.answer k (0, Sum.inl z) seed = ownGradient H G z) ∧
      (∀ k seed z, oracle.answer k (0, Sum.inr z) seed = P z)
  successful p I output law :=
    ∃ zstar, IsEquilibrium I zstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(law : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        output ω ∈ domain p ∧ ‖output ω - zstar‖ ^ 2 ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.NearZeroSumGames
